newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes up on encouraging EU rebate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes up on encouraging EU rebate.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on short covering plus an EU export rebate that was not as steep as some had expected, traders said.
"It was mainly short covering and the restitutions weren't as big as we thought they would be," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.
The EU Thursday granted ECUS of 22.35 for wheat exports. Some had expected the subsidy to total 25 ECUS.
Support also came from USDA's weekly export sales report which showed U.S. net wheat export sales for the week ending October 31 at 453,300 tonnes.
That tally was near expectations for 500,000 tonnes, the traders said.
News Turkey may be importing 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of wheat to curb high bread prices also may have lent support.

Commercial and speculative buying buoyed the market with Cargill Inc a purchaser of one million bushels of December and 300,000 bushels of March, traders said. Merrill Lynch Futures, Refco Inc and Smith Barney were noted buyers, they said. SAK Futures bought two million December, they said.
Wheat closed 5-1/2 cents higher to one cent lower, with December up 5-1/2 at $3.75.
December ended above first resistance at $3.73 and challenged the second level of $3.78-1/2 but faltered. The session high for December was $3.78-1/2.

Short term technical indicators show the market remains near oversold status with the daily relative strength index (RSI) for December closing at 37 points. The market considers an RSI of 30 or less as oversold.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 15,500 contracts, up from 13,130 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 300 March $3.70 calls and sold 300 March $3.80 calls at four cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 6,000 contracts, down from 6,229 Wednesday.
